solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Married men's nemeses who aren't slim sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A wry joke that the wife's mother is always a large, formidable figure in a husband's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' tells you to rearrange the twelve letters of WHO AREN'T SLIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses' mothers are the traditional comic enemies of husbands in British humour.

clue.text: Traveller in aircraft flew to Thailand

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
flew, as in hurried, means ran
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A passenger on a plane makes a flight to Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is someone who travels to live or work elsewhere, a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Prior to end of October draw level

indicators.note: Prior to says the word for draw comes before the other piece

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: Before late October, a contest finishes even.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one level in a stacked arrangement, as in seating or a wedding cake.

clue.text: Penetrate abdominal extremities within the gut

parts.note: to penetrate is to enter

indicators.note: extremities are the end points, so the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A medical note about piercing the edges of the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral is a medical term for the intestine, as in enteral feeding through the digestive tract.

clue.text: Changing date to Sunday reorganise details and begin journey

indicators.note: reorganise tells you to rearrange the altered word
Changing, with to, says one abbreviation is swapped for the other
to completes the swap, naming the new letter

explanation.surface: Moving a meeting to Sunday means reworking the arrangements before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping D for S makes SETAILS from DETAILS; 'reorganise' then rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a voyage, hence to start any journey.

clue.text: Batty character's regularly in your way

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here starting with the second

explanation.surface: A mad person keeps getting in your path.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is the stocking-wearing character in the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names a famous British TV character by her surname, which the clue disguises as the adjective batty.

clue.text: Sounds like a paper hankie's needed for this

definitions.text: Sounds like a paper hankie's needed for this

indicators.note: Sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: a paper hankie is a tissue

explanation.surface: A sneeze, which spoken resembles the very thing you need to catch it.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise of a sneeze, after which a tissue is needed, is written this way.

clue.text: Scary film's convincing yet it's all in the mind

parts.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's famous horror film
a convincing argument is logical

explanation.surface: A horror movie is persuasive though it only frightens your imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mental rather than physical is said to be psychological, existing only in the mind.

clue.text: Hi-fi set, both large and initially trendy, goes wrong

indicators.note: goes wrong suggests the words being scrambled into disorder
initially picks out the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stereo system, big and fashionable, breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges SET, BOTH, LARGE and T, the first letter of trendy given by 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large portable stereo player, popular in the 1980s, is a kind of hi-fi.

clue.text: Section ready to include Feds

indicators.note: to include means the word for ready takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: ready, as in all set, gives SET
Feds are FBI agents, known as G-men (government men)

explanation.surface: A group being prepared to take in some federal agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one part or portion cut off from a whole, a section of it.

clue.text: Discoloration caused by swirling rains in the centre of Eltham

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the letters taken from the place name
the centre of picks the two middle letters of the six-letter place name
swirling suggests the letters of rains being whirled around into a new order

explanation.surface: Stains on a building caused by driving rain in the south-east London district of Eltham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes ARNIS from RAINS; it sits inside TH, the centre of ELTHAM (a district of south-east London).
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnish as a noun is the dulling film or discoloured surface on metal.

clue.text: Slightly burn fish

definitions.meaning: to scorch the surface of something, blackening it lightly
a trout-like freshwater fish of cold lakes

explanation.surface: Cook a fish so that it is just a little scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the verb for scorching lightly and the name of a salmonid fish.

clue.text: Asian river is excluded from manufacturing test

indicators.note: is excluded from says the river's name is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: manufacturing, as an adjective, means industrial
the Indus is a great river of Pakistan

explanation.surface: An Asian river being barred from some factory experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is an experiment or examination to check how something performs.

clue.text: Triumph utterly obscures sound of collapse

indicators.note: obscures says the two words conceal the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A total victory drowns out the noise of something falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the dull little noise of something deflating or breaking down, as in going phut.

clue.text: Either way it's even

indicators.note: Either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, things are balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, smooth surface is both even and flat, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Swimmer had unpleasant odour

definitions.meaning: a small silvery fish of the salmon family
the past tense of the verb meaning to give off a bad whiff

explanation.surface: A swimmer who carried a nasty pong.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a small fish; the other is a British past tense of the verb meaning to stink.

clue.text: Water in old malt changing colour

indicators.note: in puts the word for water inside the rearranged malt
changing tells you the letters of malt switch into a new order

parts.note: EA is a dialect word for a river or stream of water

explanation.surface: Water added to aged malt alters its hue, as in whisky making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' turns MALT into ATML; EA goes 'in' it, after O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal names a pale greyish-beige shade, like the ground oats.

clue.text: Halt work round river in S Africa

parts.note: halt as an adjective means lame, so limp
OP is short for opus, a work
a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: Stopping a job near a river in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limpopo is the river forming South Africa's northern border with Zimbabwe and Botswana.

clue.text: Mythical musician's playing. Oh super!

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary lyre player is performing, and a listener cries out in delight.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Orpheus was the lyre player whose music charmed even the underworld.

clue.text: Stop before opening

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A command to halt ahead of a premiere or inauguration.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening.

clue.text: More than one interpretation of a Latin verse

indicators.note: interpretation of suggests the letters being read in a fresh way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem in Latin can be read with more than one meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means a few, an amount greater than one but not many.

clue.text: British beer's strong, almost menacing

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a strong, rich flavour or voice is full

explanation.surface: A potent British beer that is nearly threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful means threatening harm, as in a baleful glare.

clue.text: Penniless actor, losing heart, retrained in burlesque in Canada first of all

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled performer inside the initial letters
first of all takes the first letter of each of the last three words
retrained suggests the letters being reshaped into a new order
losing heart removes the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A broke performer, dispirited, retrains for comic theatre in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' leaves ACOR; 'retrained' gives ORAC, set 'in' BIC. Boracic is British rhyming slang: boracic lint for skint, meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Through rhyming slang the word means skint, having no money at all.

clue.text: Elaborate display of 'cool' food

parts.note: to cool something with moving air is to fan it
fare is food and drink

explanation.surface: A fancy presentation of chilled dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a showy flourish or ostentatious display, from the trumpet call.

clue.text: Plan's well-nigh perfect

definitions.note: Plan's here is plan is, the definition followed by a link

indicators.note: well-nigh means nearly, so the word falls one letter short at its end

parts.note: perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: A scheme that is very nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or scheme of action is a plan in the mind.

clue.text: Public upset after vase is stolen

indicators.note: is stolen means the vessel is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to upset a thing is to overturn it
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: People become upset after a vase goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in plain view, not hidden.

clue.text: Become submerged head to toe in black liquids

indicators.note: head to toe says the first letter is moved down to the bottom

parts.note: to become submerged is to sink

explanation.surface: Diving entirely, head to foot, into some dark fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing and printing fluids are commonly black, so these are examples of the sort.

clue.text: Touch up European holiday cottage

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tig is a children's chasing game in which you touch someone, and to tig is to touch

explanation.surface: Redecorate a holiday home in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A gîte is a French furnished house let to holidaymakers.

clue.text: Joke about lady on stage

parts.note: a gag is a joke
a, as in a. for circa, is an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A wisecrack concerning a woman performing in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gaga is the pop singer's stage name, so her surname follows Lady when she performs.

clue.text: Elite area runs new workshop

indicators.note: new says these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An exclusive district runs a new studio.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workshop.

clue.text: It's a riddle when chief replaces prince at head of procession

indicators.note: replaces says one abbreviation stands in for the other
at head of says the swap happens at the very front of the word

parts.note: a procession is a parade

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a parade whose royal leader is ousted by a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a riddle acted or described syllable by syllable, as in the parlour game.

clue.text: Chelsea exuberant after difficult race

indicators.note: after places the rearranged team name behind the word for difficult

parts.note: a steep challenge is a difficult one

indicators.note: exuberant suggests wild high spirits, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: The Chelsea football club is in high spirits after a hard-fought contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exuberant' makes LECHASE from CHELSEA (a London football club).
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race or athletics race over jumps and water.
